clue.text: Brothers and sisters in the same place on board

indicators.note: the clue's 'in' tells us one piece is set inside the other, here inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, so being on board puts you within SS
IB is short for ibidem, Latin for 'in the same place', used in footnotes

explanation.surface: Siblings sharing a cabin on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibs is informal shorthand for siblings, a collective word for brothers and sisters.

clue.text: Money taken from chapel funds

indicators.note: the letters are lifted straight out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Cash pilfered from a church collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelf is an old, disapproving word for wealth or riches, especially ill-gotten.

clue.text: King, crazy sort, the main challenger

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
a nut is slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A mad monarch who takes on the chief rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the sea: Knut (Canute) is the Danish-English king said to have ordered the tide back.
explanation.definitionFit: King Knut, also spelt Canute, is the legendary ruler who sat on the shore defying the incoming tide.

clue.text: Small change for policemen

definitions.meaning: low-value copper-coloured coins such as pennies
a British slang term for police officers

explanation.definitionFit: Coppers are both pennies and twopences, made of copper or copper-plated metal, and slang for officers of the police.

clue.text: Understand singers go off in losing the theme

parts.note: to dig something is slang for to understand or appreciate it

indicators.note: singers going off course suggests their letters wandering into a new order

explanation.surface: A listener grasps that the choir has drifted away from the melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understand' looks like a plain verb, but it is slang DIG; 'go off' is the anagram signal for the singers' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering away from the main subject of a talk is to stray off the point.

clue.text: One easily fooled by job in air-mail, originally

parts.note: a pigeon is slang for a dupe or easy mark
a post is a position of employment

explanation.surface: A gullible worker given a role in an early airmail service.
explanation.definitionFit: Before aircraft, homing birds carried messages, the first form of sending letters through the sky.

clue.text: I can get bully out-can the first bowler?

parts.note: a can is a tin
in cricket the opener is the bowler who bowls first

explanation.surface: A cricket query: could the opening bowler dismiss the bully?
explanation.walkthrough: Bully is bully beef, corned beef sold in cans; the device speaks, saying it can open the can to get the beef out.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen gadget that cuts open cans lets you get at canned corned beef.

clue.text: Latin author of "The Moon and Sixpence "?

parts.note: a full moon is a round shape, like the letter O
VI is Roman six and D the old abbreviation for a penny, from denarius

explanation.surface: A question about who wrote Somerset Maugham's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Moon and Sixpence is a novel by Somerset Maugham, which the surface leans on; here it is broken into its pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet, writer of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: I iyerpool's characters, love less, on the move?

definitions.text: iyerpool's characters, love less, on the move

indicators.note: the letters move about into a new order, as the people of the city move out

parts.note: the city's name with its S, all ten letters, are the characters to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Merseysiders leaving their city in search of new homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LIVERPOOLS, with O (love) taken away ('less'), are rearranged; 'on the move' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: Overspill is surplus population rehoused away from a crowded city, as Liverpool's was in new towns.

clue.text: Not dangerous, workin 'in office one cannot see the point of this security device

definitions.text: one cannot see the point of this security device

parts.note: safe means free of danger
typing is office work; the clipped 'workin'' drops its final G, so typing loses its G too

explanation.surface: A safe office clerk who cannot see the purpose of the security device.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'workin'' is the trick: it shows a final G dropped, so TYPING becomes TYPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastener's sharp tip is tucked under a guard, so it stays out of sight.

clue.text: Earth advanced for an immeasurably long time

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring
on means forward or advanced, as in 'later on'

explanation.surface: The planet has moved forward over vast ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an age so vast it cannot practically be measured.

clue.text: Nobleman ahead of time, practically

indicators.note: practically means almost, so the word falls just short of complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who turns up almost before he is due.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: Blade, one in heraldic gold

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a means one

explanation.surface: A sword shown on a golden coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of a rowing implement is its blade, so the word stands for the whole.

clue.text: Return of cycle outing?

parts.note: a round is a cycle, as in a round of events
a trip is an outing

explanation.surface: A bicycle excursion that comes back home.
explanation.definitionFit: A return ticket covers travel there and back, a journey ending where it started.

clue.text: Gals' recent exercising pro 13 duces regular figures

indicators.note: exercising suggests moving about, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Women who have been working out lately produce shapely figures.
explanation.walkthrough: The '13' in 'pro 13 duces' is a misprint in the paper; the word is 'produces', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblongs and squares are four-sided shapes with right angles, regular geometric figures.

clue.text: Term of reassurance when raising issue

definitions.text: Term of reassurance when raising issue

parts.words: Term of reassurance when raising issue
parts.note: issue means offspring: the cheery phrase said while lifting a toddler who has fallen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising issue' looks like bringing up a matter for discussion, but issue is a child and raising is lifting.
explanation.definitionFit: A comforting exclamation used when picking up a small child after a tumble.

clue.text: Chicken-piece for battering

definitions.meaning: the lower leg joint of a cooked fowl
a stick used to beat a drum

explanation.definitionFit: The fowl's lower leg is named after its shape, like the beater a percussionist hits a drum with.

clue.text: Square wood for window frame

parts.note: ash is a timber

explanation.surface: Squared timber bought for a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding framed part of a sash window that holds the glass.

clue.text: Performs mime, but not necessarily alfresco

definitions.text: Performs mime, but not necessarily alfresco

parts.words: Performs mime, but not necessarily alfresco
parts.note: acting a thing out in gesture; the literal reading, performing outdoors, is denied

explanation.walkthrough: Alfresco means outdoors, tempting a reading of 'performs outside'; the phrase means to show something by gestures.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise a story through movement and gesture, as in charades.

clue.text: , with National Health Insurance, have little to check

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held ', with National Health Insurance, have little to check' has lost its opening word (I, giving the first letter of I + NHI + BIT), and the correction cannot be recorded
annotationWithheld.clue: , with National Health Insurance, have little to check

clue.text: Scramble"—RAF's cue to get out of bed

indicators.note: scramble means jumble, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: The air force's command to launch fighters as the signal to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: In the RAF 'Scramble!' is the order for pilots to take off at once; here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to wake and get up, rising like a diver coming up from the depths.

clue.text: Eccentric Jack, for example

definitions.meaning: the knave is one of the court figures in a pack

explanation.definitionFit: A card is both a droll, odd character and any playing piece in a deck, such as the knave.

clue.text: Conservative member set to dismiss strikers?

parts.note: a square is someone old-fashioned and conventional
a leg is a limb, or member

explanation.surface: A Tory politician poised to sack those on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: Square leg is a cricket fielding position level with the batsman; the strikers are the batsmen, not workers on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder is placed in cricket to catch or run out the batsmen facing the bowling.

clue.text: Tree showing initial signs of elevated leaf-mould

indicators.note: initial signs are the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A tree shows early traces of leaf rot high up.
explanation.definitionFit: The elm is a tall deciduous hardwood.

clue.text: Tar-spreading skill

indicators.note: spreading tar about suggests its letters being moved into another order

explanation.surface: The craft of laying a road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Art means a skill, as in the art of conversation.

clue.text: Citrus fruit sounding nothing like a peach

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a peach is a beauty, so its opposite is ugly

explanation.surface: A citrus that seems far from lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican cross of grapefruit and tangerine with knobbly skin.

clue.text: Norman fit to become an announcer?

indicators.note: the letters are told to become something else, rearranging into a new word

explanation.surface: A man called Norman is fit for a broadcasting job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who passes on information announces it, like a newsreader telling the news.

clue.text: Sportsmen's overseas programme breaks up in total defeat

indicators.note: the tour breaking up suggests its letters falling apart and regrouping in a new order

parts.note: a tour is a team's series of matches abroad

explanation.surface: A team's foreign tour collapses in humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks up' scrambles TOUR into a new order; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing, disorderly defeat.

clue.text: Originally a father and a mother

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: The first parent was both mother and father.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Adam is the first man and so the original father.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam, the first man in Genesis, fathered the human race.

clue.text: Hardy sergeant used to weigh precious stones

definitions.meaning: Sergeant Frank ... is a dashing soldier in Thomas Hardy's novel Far from the Madding Crowd
... weight is the system for precious metals and gems

explanation.definitionFit: Troy names both Hardy's soldier and the jewellers' system of weight.

clue.text: Precise type of light for signalling

definitions.meaning: ... can mean exact, as in 'the ... spot'
a ... light is a coloured flare fired from a pistol

explanation.definitionFit: Very means exact, and a Very light is a coloured distress flare named after its inventor.

clue.text: Recoil in the air — a line has to make a fuss

parts.note: a gun's kick is its recoil
up means aloft
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A gun's kick and a falling line cause a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a noisy complaint or create a scene.
